text:
Sam: Vendor sent a new proposal — they replaced a flat reserve floor with a "sustained use ladder". attaching the short summary link: https://tiny.redwood/edp-ladder-1 :thinking_face:
Priya: can you paste the ladder numbers? need to see practical impact on our monthly burn
Sam: sure — copied from the pdf:
```
Tier A: 50% sustained use -> 20% invoice credit
Tier B: 65% sustained use -> 26% invoice credit
Tier C: 80% sustained use -> 33% invoice credit
Tier D: 95% sustained use -> 42% invoice credit
```
Sam: their definition = sustained use over billing window (30d) across committed SKUs, measured per-region. they also added a 'burst pool' carveout for extra capacity (paid at on-demand rates)
Luca: sounds like the ladder helps if our baseline is stable, but worried about preemption/allocation failures in us-west-2. do they guarantee capacity or just best-effort?
aws-sales: We can include a regional availability SLA. Proposal: 99.5% regional capacity guarantee for committed SKUs. Shortfalls → service credits (credit formula in our response doc). Can also add a quarterly reconciliation to true-up sustained tiers.
Priya: what's the shortfall credit magnitude? if we lose sustained tier mid-quarter it can blow our unit economics
aws-sales: shortfall credits: 1% of monthly committed spend per 0.1% below SLA, capped at 50% of monthly committed spend. Also offering a one-time credit for migration hours if we can't get capacity and we must move jobs to other regions.
Heather: billing question — our March invoice shows they applied Tier B credit but our reported sustained was 72% (so borderline between B and C). vendor's line item shows sustained_use_applied = 0.65 in CSV, while our usage calc is 0.72.
Heather: pasted invoice snippet:
```
2026-03-31,CommitmentCharge,SKU:gpu-p4d,qty:100,committed:100,actual_use:72,applied_tier:0.65,credit:26
```
Sam: that's the reconciliation mismatch we saw in earlier pilots — seems they floor the measurement per-availability-zone before aggregating? need to confirm aggregation method (per-az vs per-region)
Luca: action: ask them to provide raw usage histogram (daily per-SKU per-region) and the SQL they use to compute sustained %. without that we can't trust the tiering.
billing-bot: Ticket #4521 created: "EDP ladder reconciliation - provide raw usage + computation SQL" assigned to Vendor Billing Team.
aws-sales: we can supply the raw export and the calculation query. note: for multi-az customers we default to per-az cadence unless customer opts for region-aggregated measurement (can be added to contract).
Priya: negotiation points draft:
- Demand clause: mandatory region fallback within 48h or migration credits
- Measurement definition: region-aggregated sustained-use by default (not per-az)
- Preemption cap: <=5% of committed hours per month, with step credits beyond that
- True-up cadence: monthly auto-true-up with a 30d lookback window rather than quarterly
- Billing transparency: raw CSV + calc SQL shared within 72h of invoice
Luca: add request for a guaranteed 'burst pool' minimum (N GPUs) reserved for emergencies at discounted burst rate, not full on-demand. helps sudden spikes.
Heather: I'll loop in procurement + legal to get these into SOW. procurement needs sample CLA language for the measurement and credit formulas.
Sam: fine — will draft an email to vendor summarizing points and proposed contract language (I'll post later). :thumbsup:
Priya: also ask for a cap on price increases mid-term and explicit quantization/compatibility guarantees for our instance types.
aws-sales: noted. sending a revised term sheet by EOD tomorrow.
Sam: thanks — let's keep the reconciliation ticket open until we verify their raw export.
Heather: filing internal tracker: TICKET-EDP-2026-03 (procurement) — will update here.
